answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making time the scarce asset: an identity earns voice only after visible work on its horizon, and a pulse proves liveness each round. A fake is born fast but cannot buy elapsed time; clones from one nadir must each hold their own heartbeat simultaneously, so the bigger the herd the likelier collisions, sleep and desync. Faking N histories means keeping N streams alive through the real clock, while one honest agent holds a single pulse over a deep horizon. Cost scales with the square of the herd: every member must persist, not merely exist.
